warnings: Paper studies 28 different wheat genotypes - each genotype represents a separate comparison
Two growing seasons (2013-2014 and 2014-2015) - data reported separately for each year
Multiple grain fractions reported (whole grain, embryo, aleurone, endosperm) - ensure extracting whole grain Zn concentration
Paper also reports bioavailable Zn and phytate ratios which are derived measures - focus on raw grain Zn concentration
Tables show both years' data side by side - careful not to double-count
Treatment is soil application of Zn at 10 kg ha⁻¹, control is no Zn application
WARNING: SCANNED PDF - Text may have OCR errors
WARNING: VAR-UNCLEAR - Variance type not clearly stated
recon.variance_source: Table footnotes state '±SE' and data presented as 'mean ± SE' format throughout tables
recon.treatment_definition: Soil application of Zn at 10 kg ha⁻¹ as zinc sulfate (+Zn)
recon.sample_size_source: Sample size not explicitly stated in methods or tables
recon.extraction_guidance: Extract grain Zn concentration data from Table 3 only. Each of the 28 genotypes represents a separate experimental comparison between -Zn (control) and +Zn (treatment). Data is presented for both 2013-2014 and 2014-2015 growing seasons separately. Extract each genotype-year combination as a separate observation. Standard errors are provided but sample size per treatment is not stated, which limits meta-analysis utility. Focus only on whole grain Zn concentration, not the grain fraction data in Tables 5-6.

table_descriptions.Table 1: List of wheat genotypes with parentage and release information
table_descriptions.Table 2: Grain yield and protein concentration data
table_descriptions.Table 3: Grain Zn, Fe and Ca concentrations - contains PRIMARY OUTCOME
table_descriptions.Table 4: Phytate concentration, phytate/Zn ratio, and bioavailable Zn
table_descriptions.Table 5: Zn, Fe, Ca concentrations in embryo and aleurone fractions
table_descriptions.Table 6: Zn, Fe, Ca concentrations in endosperm fraction
table_descriptions.Table 7: AFLP primer evaluation for genetic diversity

recon.extraction_method_reason: Scanned/image tables - use vision to supplement text
challenge_hints: Verify all numbers carefully - OCR may confuse 0/O, 1/l/I
If numbers look wrong, flag for manual review
Check Methods section for 'mean ± SE' or 'mean ± SD' statement
Check table footnotes for variance definitions
